## Demo scenarios (generated)

Search: every curated site, baseline landings daily from 2027-01-01 to the end of the ephemeris, slips of 1-30 days later. Mission 14 days, observer 2 m, Sun threshold 0.5, Earth margin 1.0° (app defaults). Ranking score is **Both** (Sun and Earth link). The search uses hourly samples; the numbers below are the 1-minute reference (`golden.py`) and agree with the TS engine to the parity tolerances in SPEC.md (checked against `golden.json`).

### Rank flips: the best site changes after a slip

A flip needs the winner to lead by at least 10 points before the slip and trail by at least that much after it. Flips come from distinct places (sites within 40 km count as one) where enough exist.

**1. IM-2 Athena (Mons Mouton) vs Shackleton–de Gerlache connecting ridge**: slip 15 days, landing 2029-02-20 → 2029-03-07. Gap in Both %: +51.2 → -61.7 (swing 112.9 points).

| | Site | Landing (UTC 00:00) | Sunlit | Earth link | Both | First sunset |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| baseline | IM-2 Athena (Mons Mouton) (`mons-mouton-im2`) | 2029-02-20 | 77.2% | 55.4% | **51.2%** | 273.4 h |
| baseline | Shackleton–de Gerlache connecting ridge (`connecting-ridge`) | 2029-02-20 | 7.5% | 24.8% | **0.0%** | 183.9 h |
| slip +15 d | IM-2 Athena (Mons Mouton) (`mons-mouton-im2`) | 2029-03-07 | 0.0% | 100.0% | **0.0%** | no sunlight |
| slip +15 d | Shackleton–de Gerlache connecting ridge (`connecting-ridge`) | 2029-03-07 | 61.7% | 79.5% | **61.7%** | 329.9 h |

Reproduce: sites `mons-mouton-im2` + `connecting-ridge`, duration 14 d, landing 2029-02-20T00:00:00Z, slip slider +15 d.

## The 3D beat (UI v2, hand-written; outside the generated block)

Run after any scenario above. The default tab is **3D Terrain**.

1. **See the terrain.** The south pole renders from the LOLA 80 m display DEM (×3 vertical, labelled "display only"). Shadows are the engine's own Sun/horizon state from the 2 km horizon grid. Beacons show each site's state in words (`SUN + EARTH`, `SUN ONLY`, `EARTH ONLY`, `NO SUN, NO EARTH`), computed from the site's own finer horizon.
2. **Press Play** (6 h/s). Shadows sweep and beacons flip as the timeline's windows open and close; the timeline and panorama follow the same cursor.
3. **Slip the landing** with the Days slider. The shadows and beacons update without a visible stall.
4. **Switch to Surface.** The first-person skyline shows the Sun disk dropping behind the ridge in the same frame the timeline says blocked (`SUN BLOCKED · ridge at az …`).
5. **Overlays.** PGDA Sun/Earth (NASA long-term averages) and Window Sun/Earth/Both (scored for the mission window from the 2 km grid, labelled grid-approximate) are draped on the terrain. The Map tab shows the same layers in 2D.

Screenshots: [3D live shadows](img/ui-v2/terrain-1440-live-shadows.jpg), [3D PGDA Sun](img/ui-v2/terrain-1440-pgda-sun.jpg), [Surface](img/ui-v2/surface-1440.jpg), [Map, Window Sun](img/ui-v2/map-1440-window-sun.jpg).

Measured in Chrome on the dev server (Apple Silicon, 2 sites × 14 d): Play 60 fps (worst frame 17.7 ms); slip step with 3D visible, synchronous commit median 8.3 ms, max 12.3 ms; window scoring 0.4 s compute (0.8 s including the 300 ms debounce). Transfer sizes on the Vercel preview (brotli): `grid-horizons.bin` 11.9 MB → 4.75 MB, `terrain-display.bin` 2.1 MB → 1.78 MB, both streamed after first paint; first paint is about 1.5 MB (JS 86 kB, `ephemeris.bin` 1.40 MB).
